B is clearly better.

B's extra details are accurate: 310 votes in the first ballot, 316 needed, 325 in the second, and a CDU/CSU–SPD coalition. But the question only asks who became chancellor. Both answers correctly name Friedrich Merz, elected on 6 May 2025 to succeed Scholz. A adds accurate detail: he got 310 votes in the first ballot and 325 in the second, was the first post-war candidate to lose a first-round vote, and leads a CDU/CSU–SPD coalition. It lists unrelated sources (the 2016, 2021 and 2026 prizes), which weakens its grounding a little. A is more complete and more useful.

Its sources back these claims. A is correct but bare, and it lists sources it never uses, such as Super Bowl LI. B is the more useful answer.

Answer A adds details its sources appear to support: the 29–13 score over the Patriots, the date, Levi's Stadium, Kenneth Walker III as MVP and Seattle's second title. Answer B is correct but very thin, and it lists unused sources like Super Bowl LI. A is more complete and useful.

B's figures match the final table: Norway 41 medals (18-12-11), USA second with 12 golds and 33 medals. B is accurate and well-sourced.

Both answers correctly name Norway. A's figures (18 gold, 41 medals in total, a record that beats the 16 golds from 2022, and the USA second with 12) match the final table as I remember it, and A covers the question fully. B gives 17 golds, which looks wrong. B's 10 golds for Italy is plausible, but its main number is off.

Both answers correctly name Lando Norris and McLaren's first drivers' title since 2008. B adds accurate detail: third place in Abu Dhabi, a 423–421 margin over Verstappen, Piastri still in contention, the end of Verstappen's four-title run, and Norris as the eleventh British champion. Both correctly name Lando Norris. A adds accurate, useful context: he won 423 to 421 over Verstappen after finishing third in Abu Dhabi, Piastri was still in contention, and it was McLaren's first drivers' title since 2008. B is correct but minimal and lists sources it never cites. A is more complete and still concise.

Both correctly name Carlos Alcaraz, who beat Djokovic in the final. B adds details that check out: the score 2–6, 6–2, 6–3, 7–5, the February 1 date, his first Australian Open title, the youngest man to complete the career Grand Slam, and Djokovic denied a 25th major. A adds accurate details: the score (2–6, 6–2, 6–3, 7–5), the date (February 1), that this completed his career Grand Slam as the youngest man to do it, and that it stopped Djokovic's bid for a 25th major. Both are accurate. A is correct but thin, and it slightly overstates that alligators' teeth are 'all hidden'. B covers the snout, a more accurate teeth description, salt glands, range and colour, all supported by its cited sources. That makes B more complete and more useful.

A is accurate and covers snout, teeth, salt glands, habitat and color, with source support. B is shorter and wrongly says all of an alligator's teeth are hidden when its mouth is closed; only the lower teeth are. B also leaves out habitat and salt tolerance.

B is thin and has errors: it says resin is "extruded" (it isn't) and uses an odd, dated "as of 2019" reference. It also gives little detail on the different methods.

Answer B is accurate, cites relevant sources and adds useful details such as the Buda/Pest split and the Danube Delta.

A adds accurate, sourced details: the Buda/Pest split, about 2,850 km of river through ten countries, and the delta on the Romania–Ukraine border. B pads its answer with unrelated rivers, cites irrelevant sources and falls back on general knowledge. It is honest about that, but it is cluttered and less useful.

The extra details about the homemade computer and the hacking ban are accurate. It also lists Emanuel School, which is his secondary school, not a university. B is accurate but less clear and less complete.

Both answers correctly name the Cambodian riel. B also explains that US dollars are widely used, gives the exchange rate, and offers practical tips, all backed by fitting sources. B covers anatta vs atman but leaves out the founder, the rejection of the Vedas and caste. It pads with follower counts, and its claim about shared deities is a weak framing.

Its point about stiff controls is muddled and beside the point, the line about wealthy passengers is filler, and it lists source [2] without ever citing it.

B rightly says no one created government, explains how it arose in early civilisations, and names the first theorists (Plato, Aristotle, Hobbes). Its 3600 BCE kingship date is uncertain. A skips ancient origins, wrongly ties self-government to 17th-century "democratic republics", and never uses source [1].

B suggests the concept took shape with Hobbes and Locke, which ignores thousands of years of earlier government. A wrongly says baking soda reacts just from getting wet, when it actually needs an acid. A also presents two-stage action as true of all baking powder. B correctly explains the role of acid and what double-acting means, and gives practical guidance on using both and on substitution. B is clearer and more accurate.

B wrongly says baking soda reacts just from getting wet, when it actually needs an acid. B also presents double action as true of all baking powder, and its sources are thin.

A also never gives drip figures. B is accurate and consistent. It covers per-ounce and per-serving amounts and a double shot, and it says the numbers vary.
